summary: Ferry County camp in 1929, then a 10-foot pole L-5 tower built 1935; used by the AWS in 1942; gone by the 1940s (sources split removed vs destroyed); no current site description.

facts.design: 10-foot pole tower with an L-5 cab
facts.status_note: Tower and cab gone by the 1940s; FFLOS says removed and Willhite says destroyed; no source describes the site today

staffing.status: Used by the AWS from March 27 to May 9, 1942; no other staffing in the sources read

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and Washington Lookouts say removed in the 1940s; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed in the 1940s. All put the end after the 1945 survey.
The 1934 panoramas call it Thirteen Mile Ridge; a 1936 survey gives Thirteen Mile Mountain; the record uses Thirteenmile Mountain.

notes_for_editor: No source read describes the site today. A Ranger page lists a 2.0-mile Thirteenmile Lookout Road in Colville National Forest, and a WTA page describes a Thirteenmile trail from the San Poil River; neither is tied to this lookout, so neither is cited. The AWS acronym is not expanded in any source read. The brief has no height, so height_m comes from the 10-foot pole tower. The two 1946 events are placeholder years for 'the 1940s'.
